name: Polyphenylene sulfide
description: Polyphenylene sulfide (CAS 25212-74-2 ), commonly abbreviated as PPS, is a high-performance engineering thermoplastic used across demanding industrial sectors. Poly(thio-1,4-phenylene) is a recognized alternative designation in technical and polymer literature. It delivers exceptional chemical resistance and dimensional stability under continuous high-temperature service conditions. This makes it a preferred matrix resin for precision-engineered components in various heavy industries. In automotive manufacturing, PPS is compounded into glass- or mineral-filled grades for fuel system components and pump housings. These under-hood parts must withstand aggressive fluids and elevated temperatures consistently. Electronics manufacturers rely on it for connector housings, relay components, and SMT-compatible parts. In these applications, tight dimensional tolerances and flame resistance are critical for safety and performance. Aerospace and defense applications include structural brackets, fluid handling components, and radomes. These parts require low weight combined with extreme thermal and chemical durability in harsh environments. It is also processed into films, fibers, and coatings for industrial filtration membranes and specialty textile applications. PPS is supplied as pellets or granules, with compounded grades available for specific targets. Standard commercial grades are differentiated by melt flow, crosslink level, and filler content rather than pharmacopeial specifications. Technical-grade material is the primary market form for most industrial users. Specialty grades are available for injection molding, extrusion, and compression molding processes.
